questions.q: Asked at interfaith meetings about Islam’s “hierarchy,” what does the editorial say serves as the source of religious guidance?
options: A single hereditary office
Not quite. The article says: The Quran and the Prophet’s example, which every believer is encouraged to study – there is no central chain of command.
The ruler of each country
Not quite. The article says: The Quran and the Prophet’s example, which every believer is encouraged to study – there is no central chain of command.
A council elected every few years
Not quite. The article says: The Quran and the Prophet’s example, which every believer is encouraged to study – there is no central chain of command.
The Quran and the Prophet’s example, which every believer is encouraged to study – there is no central chain of command
Yes. Scholars explain; they do not rule.
questions.rationale: “The Quran and the practical model of conduct established by the Prophet Muhammad… serve as the fountainhead of religious guidance. There is no centralized authority.”

questions.q: What does the editorial say the Prophet did whenever he had to choose between two courses?
options: He put off the choice
Not quite. The article says: He chose the easier.
He chose the easier
Right. “God desires ease for you, not hardship.”
He let others decide
Not quite. The article says: He chose the easier.
He chose the harder, as a discipline
Not quite. The article says: He chose the easier.
questions.rationale: “Whenever the Prophet had to choose between two options, he always chose the easier.”

questions.q: The Wright brothers, bicycle makers working quietly, flew first; a famous scientist with funds and publicity did not. What does the article conclude?
options: Scientists should not attempt inventions
Not quite. The article says: Great success needs steady focus and perseverance; attention before the work is done only hinders.
Great success needs steady focus and perseverance; attention before the work is done only hinders
Well read. They shunned publicity until they had something to show.
Publicity is essential from the start
Not quite. The article says: Great success needs steady focus and perseverance; attention before the work is done only hinders.
Small workshops are better than laboratories
Not quite. The article says: Great success needs steady focus and perseverance; attention before the work is done only hinders.
questions.rationale: “Great success demands unwavering focus, dedication, perseverance, and hard work. Public attention, before the task is accomplished, will only act as hindrance.”

questions.q: Listening to the river at night amid mountains, trees and stars, what “message” did the speaker hear in nature?
options: Blessed are those who live together in peace and harmony – unity amid diversity
Yes. Togetherness is the culture of the universe.
The strong survive and the weak perish
Not quite. The article says: Blessed are those who live together in peace and harmony – unity amid diversity.
Nothing lasts, so nothing matters
Not quite. The article says: Blessed are those who live together in peace and harmony – unity amid diversity.
Each must look after himself
Not quite. The article says: Blessed are those who live together in peace and harmony – unity amid diversity.
questions.rationale: “I felt that it was conveying this universal message: Blessed are those who live together in peace and harmony.”

questions.q: What, according to the speech, is the one difference between man and the rest of the universe in following this harmony?
options: Man follows it only in groups
Not quite. The article says: The universe follows it by compulsion; man must follow it by choice – and in this lies his greatness.
Man is exempt from it
Not quite. The article says: The universe follows it by compulsion; man must follow it by choice – and in this lies his greatness.
The universe follows it by compulsion; man must follow it by choice – and in this lies his greatness
Correct. Freedom gives the act its worth.
The universe follows it less perfectly
Not quite. The article says: The universe follows it by compulsion; man must follow it by choice – and in this lies his greatness.
questions.rationale: “What the rest of the world is following under compulsion, man has to follow by his own choice. Herein lies the greatness of man.”

questions.q: A man who had been his country’s richest died its second richest. What does the article say death teaches everyone?
options: Each thinks himself “first” until death shows that God alone is the reality – wise is he who learns it beforehand
Right. Death is the most ruthless of teachers.
Business is too risky to pursue
Not quite. The article says: Each thinks himself “first” until death shows that God alone is the reality – wise is he who learns it beforehand.
Rankings are always inaccurate
Not quite. The article says: Each thinks himself “first” until death shows that God alone is the reality – wise is he who learns it beforehand.
Wealth should be spent quickly
Not quite. The article says: Each thinks himself “first” until death shows that God alone is the reality – wise is he who learns it beforehand.
questions.rationale: “Death brings the message that the only reality is that of God; no other ‘I’ has any real existence. Death is the most ruthless of teachers.”

questions.q: A man showed Caliph Harun al-Rashid an astonishing trick of threading needles in mid-air. What did the Caliph say as he rewarded him?
options: “You are the wisest man in my court”
Not quite. The article says: “If only you had developed this skill in some useful work”.
“Perform it again tomorrow”
Not quite. The article says: “If only you had developed this skill in some useful work”.
“Teach this to my soldiers”
Not quite. The article says: “If only you had developed this skill in some useful work”.
“If only you had developed this skill in some useful work”
Yes. Cleverness is not the same as real work.
questions.rationale: “Harun al-Rashid… said, ‘Woe unto you, if only you had developed this skill in some useful work.’”

questions.q: The article says every injunction has something written “between the lines.” What is unstated in the simple words “Speak the truth”?
options: “…unless others disagree”
Not quite. The article says: “…even if the truth appears harmful to you”.
“…even if the truth appears harmful to you”
Well reasoned. The sacrifice involved is left for us to infer.
“…when it is convenient”
Not quite. The article says: “…even if the truth appears harmful to you”.
“…to those who ask politely”
Not quite. The article says: “…even if the truth appears harmful to you”.
questions.rationale: “When the simple words ‘Speak the truth’ are uttered, what they really mean is: ‘Speak the truth, even if the truth appears harmful to you.’”

questions.q: “Those who listen to what is said and follow what is best in it” (39:18). What does the article call the first condition of such right thinking?
options: To agree with the majority
Not quite. The article says: To be objective – free of bias and prejudice, able to tell the relevant from the irrelevant.
To have a good memory
Not quite. The article says: To be objective – free of bias and prejudice, able to tell the relevant from the irrelevant.
To be objective – free of bias and prejudice, able to tell the relevant from the irrelevant
Exactly. Meaning depends on the listener’s mind.
To listen only to the learned
Not quite. The article says: To be objective – free of bias and prejudice, able to tell the relevant from the irrelevant.
questions.rationale: “The first condition of right thinking is that you should be objective and be free of all kinds of bias and prejudices.”

questions.q: The Quran calls the Day of Judgement “the Day of loss and gain.” What does the commentary say people will find then?
options: What was counted as gain in this world may prove loss, and what seemed loss may prove real gain
Well read. The standard there is moral, not material.
Everyone will be judged by his wealth
Not quite. The article says: What was counted as gain in this world may prove loss, and what seemed loss may prove real gain.
Losses will be repaid in money
Not quite. The article says: What was counted as gain in this world may prove loss, and what seemed loss may prove real gain.
Nothing done here will matter
Not quite. The article says: What was counted as gain in this world may prove loss, and what seemed loss may prove real gain.
questions.rationale: “Gaining, which was considered as such will actually turn out to be losing, while what was considered as losing will turn out to be gaining in the real sense.”
